headline: GEM NO. 2 oil spill contained, no new leakage
dek: [VERIFIED FACT] UAE authorities say the GEM NO. 2 oil leak is stopped/contained with no new leakage detected; specialist teams are repairing damaged sections, restoring systems and assessing structural integrity to decide the safest handling option; beach closures are precautionary.
sources: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure / Ministry of Climate Change and Environment / NCEMA via WAM, Oct 30; Reuters, Oct 30
fault_line: The war's environmental bill comes ashore -- who pays for a spill from a struck tanker in Gulf waters, and how far does it spread?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT] UAE authorities say the GEM NO. 2 oil leak is stopped/contained with no new leakage detected; specialist teams are repairing damaged sections, restoring systems and assessing structural integrity to decide the safest handling option; beach closures are precautionary. [VERIFIED FACT] Latest satellite imagery: slick concentrated off Umm Al Quwain, extending partly toward Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Sharjah. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Reuters shipping sources: the vessel was struck by a projectile on Oct 9, causing a fire later extinguished; authorities have not stated the cause.
sections.what_verified: WAM official statement + Reuters wire + The National (T2) + Peninsula/ARN News relays all agree on containment, no new leakage and slick location.
sections.what_disputed: Cause of the incident is NOT officially stated -- the Oct 9 projectile strike is shipping-source attribution via Reuters only. Cleanup is ongoing, not complete: field surveys, monitoring and coastal cleaning continue, and the vessel's final handling option is undecided pending structural assessment.
sections.why_matters: The Hormuz war just washed up on UAE beaches -- the slick is contained, but the tanker that was hit on Oct 9 still has no safe way forward.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (WAM Oct 30 19:19 , absent from Oct 30/31 scans) -- UAE: GEM NO. 2 oil spill contained, no new leakage; slick concentrated off Umm Al Quwain extending toward Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman, Sharjah; tanker struck by projectile Oct 9 per Reuters shipping sources

totw_analysis: Our read: The Hormuz war just washed up on UAE beaches -- the slick is contained, but the tanker that was hit on Oct 9 still has no safe way forward. The fault line our audience is arguing over: The war's environmental bill comes ashore -- who pays for a spill from a struck tanker in Gulf waters, and how far does it spread?
